tasks.title: Load and validate config.toml
steps: Write TS-11-9, 10, 11, 12, 15, 16 as table-driven tests named like TestXxx_TS_11_N in internal/service/config/config_test.go (t.TempDir, t.Setenv, t.Chdir) and confirm they fail
Promote github.com/BurntSushi/toml v1.6.0 to a direct requirement in go.mod (go mod tidy)

Define Config{Server{Listen}, Hub{URL, AuthCacheTTL time.Duration}, Database{Path}, Secrets{KeyFile}} with toml tags; decode the TTL from a string via time.ParseDuration so a non-duration string fails naming hub.auth_cache_ttl

Implement Load(explicit string) (Config, error): lookup order --config, ./config.toml, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/agent-fox/config.toml, $HOME/.config/agent-fox/config.toml; when none exists list every path tried; a TOML syntax error names the file and line/column (toml.ParseError)
After toml.DecodeFile refuse every md.Undecoded() key naming key.String(); map toml type errors to the dotted key where possible, falling back to the key from the error message

Expand ${NAME} (regexp [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*) in every string value after decoding via os.LookupEnv; an unset variable errors naming the variable and the dotted key; set-but-empty expands to empty; a bare $ is left alone
Apply defaults (listen 127.0.0.1:8090, ttl 60s, database.path from XDG_STATE_HOME or $HOME/.local/state/agent-fox/agent-fox.db) with a small XDG helper using os.UserHomeDir

Validate: hub.url required, absolute http/https, no query/fragment, trailing / dropped, path prefix kept; secrets.key_file required non-empty; ttl in [1s,15m] never clamped; server.listen passes net.SplitHostPort; every error names the dotted key

Resolve relative database.path and secrets.key_file against the config file's directory, returning absolute paths; expose a helper reporting whether hub.url is http with a non-loopback host (used later for the WARN)
Return plain errors only: no os.Exit, no toolio import

tasks.title: Load the key file and seal/open workspace tokens
steps: Write TS-11-18..22 in internal/service/secrets/secrets_test.go (the property test seeds a math/rand source from the test and logs the seed) and confirm they fail
Implement LoadKey(path) (Key, error): os.ReadFile, trim whitespace, base64.StdEncoding decode, require exactly 32 bytes; every error names the path and reason and never includes file contents
On non-Windows refuse info.Mode().Perm()&0o077 != 0 with an error naming the file and its octal mode; accept 0600, 0400, 0700 (use a build-tagged helper or runtime.GOOS check)
Implement Key.Seal(slug, token) []byte: AES-256-GCM, fresh 12-byte nonce from crypto/rand, additional data "agent-fox/subscription/"+slug, output = 0x01 || nonce || ciphertext+tag

Implement Key.Open(slug, sealed) (string, error): reject length < 1+12+16, unknown version byte, wrong key, altered byte or other slug with errors; never panic and never return plaintext on error; errors never include token or key bytes
Expose sentinel error ErrUnreadable-style wrapping so the store can classify failures with errors.Is
Keep Key's String/GoString/Format redacted so the key cannot be logged by accident

tasks.title: Open the SQLite state store with migrations and subscription persistence
steps: Write TS-11-24, 25, 26, 29, 70 in internal/service/store/store_test.go and confirm they fail
Add modernc.org/sqlite to go.mod/go.sum (go get modernc.org/sqlite; pin a version) and blank-import it in the store package

Implement Open(ctx, path, key secrets.Key) (*Store, error): MkdirAll parent 0700, create the file with 0600 when missing, open with DSN file:<path>?_pragma=busy_timeout(5000)&_pragma=journal_mode(WAL)&_pragma=foreign_keys(1); verify the pragmas hold on a fresh pooled connection; errors name the path

Migrations: an ordered append-only []string; af_schema_migrations(version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, applied_at TEXT); apply each unapplied one in its own transaction; never touch PRAGMA user_version or any table not prefixed af_
If the recorded max version exceeds the known count fail naming both versions and leave the file unchanged (check before writing anything)
Migration 1: af_subscriptions(slug TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, label_prefix, sealed_token BLOB, token_user TEXT NULL, subscribed_by, created_at, updated_at as RFC 3339 UTC)

Implement Upsert(ctx, slug, labelPrefix, token, tokenUser, subscribedBy, now) (sub Subscription, created bool, err error) as one INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(slug) DO UPDATE statement that keeps created_at; Get, List (sorted by slug), Delete (reports whether a row existed)
Subscription carries TokenState computed by opening the sealed token with the key ('ok' or 'unreadable'); the type exposes no token or ciphertext
Implement Token(ctx, slug) (string, error) returning the opened PAT; errors ErrNotSubscribed and ErrUnreadable (errors.Is) with no plaintext in either
Expose DB() *sql.DB, Ping(ctx) and Close()

tasks.title: Build the hub client and the fakehub test double
steps: Write TS-11-71 and TS-11-72 in internal/hub/fakehub/fakehub_test.go and TS-11-30..36 in internal/hub/client_test.go and confirm they fail

Implement internal/hub/fakehub mirroring internal/triage/fakeforge: New(t testing.TB) *Hub with URL, httptest.Server and t.Cleanup; AddUser(token, userID, slugs), AddWorkspaceToken(token, slugs), Count(path, tokenHash), Requests() in order, Fail(path, status), FailOnce, Hangup(path), Delay(path, d), Clear(); a token hash helper (hex sha256); /api/v1/user answers {id, login} or 401; /api/v1/workspaces/{slug} answers 200 or 403 for a known token not seeing it, 401 for an unknown token
Implement internal/hub Client{BaseURL, HTTP *http.Client, UserAgent} via New(baseURL, version); HTTP has a 10s timeout and CheckRedirect returning http.ErrUseLastResponse

User(ctx, token) (User{ID, Login}, error) and Workspace(ctx, token, slug) error: GET <base>/api/v1/user and <base>/api/v1/workspaces/<url.PathEscape(slug)> (set URL.RawPath so %2F survives), headers Authorization Bearer, Accept application/json, User-Agent agent-fox/<version>
Read at most 1 MiB via io.LimitReader; id accepted as JSON string or number (json.Number kept as decimal string), empty id is unavailable; body not a JSON object is unavailable
Status map: user 200 ok, 401/403 refused, 404/3xx/429/5xx/other unavailable; workspace 200 found, 401 refused, 403/404 not found, others unavailable

Errors: sentinels ErrRefused and ErrNotFound plus *UnavailableError{Status, Err} usable with errors.Is/errors.As; transport errors are unwrapped from *url.Error so no URL or token ends up in a message; assert in a property test (seeded from the test) that err.Error() never contains the token
Only this package names hub paths and the user id field

tasks.title: Build the HTTP surface: probes, error envelope, panic recovery, request logging
steps: Write TS-11-47, 48, 51, 52 in internal/service/api/server_test.go using httptest and a captured slog JSON buffer, and confirm they fail

Export the full version document from internal/toolio (e.g. func (a *App) VersionDocument() any or a package-level function returning the five-field struct) keeping Identity and the ldflags-then-build-info rule unchanged; the api package takes the document as an injected value so it never imports cmd

Create internal/service/api with errors.go: Code constants and the status table (invalid_request 400, unauthenticated 401, not_found 404, method_not_allowed 405, payload_too_large 413, unsupported_media_type 415, invalid_hub_token 422, internal 500, hub_unavailable 502, not_ready 503) and writeError emitting application/json {"error":{"code","message"}} with no error_type

Add JSON body helper decodeBody(w, r, v): Content-Type via mime.ParseMediaType == application/json else 415; http.MaxBytesReader 64 KiB (413 on *http.MaxBytesError); DisallowUnknownFields; trailing data check; malformed/unknown/trailing give 400 invalid_request

Server: ServeMux with method patterns; GET /healthz {"status":"ok"}; GET /readyz pings the store ({"status":"ready"} or 503 not_ready); GET /version; custom handling so an unknown route is 404 not_found and a wrong method is 405 method_not_allowed in the envelope

Middleware chain: recover (500 internal, slog ERROR with debug.Stack in a stack attribute, no panic text in the response) and an access logger emitting one record msg 'request' with method, path, status, duration and user (only when known, set through a request-scoped holder); never log Authorization, bodies, tokens, ciphertext or the key
NewServer(deps) returns *http.Server with ReadHeaderTimeout > 0 (e.g. 10s); keep a hook to register extra routes so tests can add a panicking route

tasks.title: Authenticate callers and check workspace visibility through hub with TTL caches
steps: Write TS-11-45 and TS-11-46 (property, run under -race) in internal/service/ttl/ttl_test.go and TS-11-37..40, 42, 43 in internal/service/api/auth_test.go using fakehub, an injected clock and a trivial authed route, and confirm they fail

Implement internal/service/ttl: generic Cache[V] with New(capacity, ttl, now func() time.Time), Get, Put, Delete, DeleteIf(pred), Len; mutex-protected; at capacity evict expired entries first, then the oldest; never return an entry after its TTL

Implement the auth component in internal/service/api: identity cache keyed by hex sha256 of the token holding {userID} or a refusal; visibility cache keyed by (token hash, slug) holding found or not-found; both capacity 10,000 and TTL from config

Middleware for /api/v1/*: parse Authorization (scheme case-insensitive Bearer, non-empty token) else 401 unauthenticated with no hub call; identity hit or call hub User; refused is cached and answers 401; unavailable is never cached and answers 502 hub_unavailable; store the user id on the request context and in the log holder

Slug routes: validate ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,99}$ first (400 invalid_request, before identity), then identity, then visibility via hub Workspace with the caller token: found passes, not found is cached and answers 404 not_found, unavailable is not cached and answers 502
A hub ErrRefused (401) on any call made with the caller's token evicts that token's identity entry and all its visibility entries (DeleteIf on the token hash) and answers 401 unauthenticated
Expose a Visible(ctx, token, slug) (bool, error) helper that routes and list handlers reuse, and a separate PAT path that calls the hub client directly and never touches either cache
Make the clock injectable through the server dependencies so tests advance it without sleeping

tasks.title: Implement PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{slug} subscribe
steps: Write the tests in internal/service/api/subscribe_test.go with fakehub, a real store in t.TempDir() and a generated key, and confirm they fail
Register PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{slug} behind the slug and identity middleware

Decode {hub_token string, label_prefix *string} with the shared body helper (415/413/400 before any write); hub_token must be non-empty; label_prefix defaults to af: and must be 1-32 characters with no whitespace, control character or comma, else 400 invalid_request and no hub call with the PAT

Gate call: hub Workspace with the PAT using the client directly (never the caches): ErrRefused gives 422 invalid_hub_token saying hub refused the token; ErrNotFound gives 422 invalid_hub_token naming the slug; unavailable gives 502 hub_unavailable
Then best-effort hub User with the PAT: a user gives token_user, ErrRefused leaves it empty, unavailable gives 502 hub_unavailable; the gate runs strictly before the user call

Seal and upsert in one statement via the store, with subscribed_by = the caller's user id from context; respond 201 on create and 200 on replace with the subscription view JSON (slug, label_prefix, token_user null when empty, subscribed_by, token_state, created_at, updated_at)
Replace semantics: absent label_prefix resets to af:, token_user replaced by this request's answer, created_at kept, updated_at now (injected clock)
Verify nothing is written on any failure and neither cache is read, filled or evicted by PAT calls, even when the PAT equals the caller's token
Property test TS-11-62 (seeded from the test): for random PATs, slugs and prefixes scan the .db file, the -wal file and every response body for the PAT bytes

steps: Write the tests in cmd/agent-fox/start_test.go (binary-level ones use the buildBinary helper, fakehub and temp dirs; TS-11-8 calls the run function with an injected failing net.Listener) and confirm they fail
